lessons.title: Words: people you meet
note: These words come up when you meet someone. 方 is a polite word for 人: あの方, “that person”. どなた is a polite だれ, “who”.
Age uses 年 (とし). Twenty is special: 二十歳, read はたち. ええ is a relaxed はい.

私 は 留学生 です

lessons.title: も and と: too, and
lessons.pattern: X も Y です · X と Y
note: も means “too” or “also”, and it takes the place of は: 私も学生です, “I'm a student too.” With a negative it means “either”: 私も学生ではありません, “I'm not a student either.”
と joins nouns into a complete list, like “and”: 本とペン, “a book and a pen”. It only joins nouns, never whole sentences.

examples.t: 私 も 学生 です
これ は 本 と ノート です
examples.en: These are a book and a notebook.

examples.t: 田中 さん も 学生 ではありません
examples.en: Mr Tanaka isn't a student either.

w.を: を marks what a verb acts on.

drills.note: も replaces は to add “too”.

w.の: の would make it “the book's notebook”.

drills.c: 私 ___ 医者 ではありません
drills.label: Choose the particle

w.と: と joins nouns. “Either” is も.

lessons.title: Words: things you carry
note: これ, それ, あれ and どれ stand alone. この, その, あの and どの need a noun after them: この傘, “this umbrella”.
These are everyday things to point at and ask about. 物 means “thing”, as in 私の物, “my things”.

w.これ: これ means “this one”, not “which one”.

lessons.title: Words: shopping
note: いくら asks a price, and いくつ asks how many. 全部で means “all together”: 全部でいくらですか.
Japanese money counts in 万 (10,000): 一万円 is ten thousand yen. 八百屋 is a fruit and vegetable shop.

lessons.title: ごろ, ね and よ
lessons.pattern: X時 ごろ · Y です ね · Y です よ
note: ごろ after a time means “about”: 七時ごろ, “around seven”. Use it for a point in time. For an amount of time you'll use ぐらい, which comes later.
ね at the end asks the listener to agree, like “isn't it?”: いい時計ですね. よ tells them something they may not know, like “you know”: 明日は休みですよ.

examples.t: 今 三時 ごろ です
今日 は 休み です ね
examples.en: Today's a day off, isn't it?

examples.t: 銀行 は 三時 まで です よ
examples.en: The bank is open until three, you know.

drills.note: よ passes on news the listener may not know.

lessons.title: Words: times and dates
note: The days of the month have their own readings for the 1st to the 10th, and the 20th: 二日 (ふつか), 三日 (みっか), 八日 (ようか), 二十日 (はつか). The 1st is 一日, read ついたち. From the 11th on, it's just the number plus にち: 十一日.
朝, 昼 and 晩 split the day. 夜 is night, and ゆうべ is last night.

examples.t: 誕生日 は 三月 三日 です
あさって は 休み です

lessons.title: Words: meals and mornings
note: Meals are built on ご飯: 朝ご飯 (breakfast), 昼ご飯 (lunch) and 晩ご飯 (dinner). ご飯 alone means cooked rice, or a meal.
Morning verbs: 起きる (get up), 顔を洗う (wash your face), 歯を磨く (brush your teeth), シャワーを浴びる (take a shower). お in お茶 and お菓子 makes them sound polite.

lessons.title: Words: free time
note: Many activities are a noun plus します: 勉強します (study), 料理します (cook), 掃除します (clean), 洗濯します (do the laundry), 散歩します (take a walk), 練習します (practise).
You can also put を between them: 掃除をします. Both are fine. 習う is learning from a teacher, like ピアノを習います.

lessons.title: Words: getting around
note: You ride with に: バスに乗ります, “get on the bus”. You get off with を: 電車を降ります. で marks the vehicle as the way you go: 自転車で行きます.
出かける is going out of the house. 着く is arriving, and the place takes に: 駅に着きました.

lessons.title: ましょうか: shall I? shall we?
note: ましょうか offers help: かばんを持ちましょうか, “Shall I carry your bag?” 窓を開けましょうか, “Shall I open the window?”
It also asks what to do together: 何を食べましょうか, “What shall we eat?” To turn down an offer politely, say いいえ、大丈夫です.

lessons.title: Words: around town
note: Places to know in a Japanese town: 郵便局 (post office), 交番 (police box, for directions and lost things), 喫茶店 (an old-style café), 食堂 (a cheap canteen).
いかがですか is the polite どうですか: コーヒーはいかがですか, “Would you like a coffee?” 遊ぶ is to hang out or play, for adults too.
